cases.title: Hunan Urban Development: a man tried to kill himself after his house was added to the plant site
cases.place: Changsha, Xiangtan and Zhuzhou municipalities and the Zhaoshan area, Hunan, China; the recorded non-compliance is at the Changshanyuan wastewater treatment plant in Changsha
cases.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on the city of Changsha. The works ran along the Changsha-Zhuzhou-Xiangtan flood control and landscape road corridor in six sections - Changsha, Xiangtan urban area, Zhaoshan, Zhuzhou, Zhuzhou Leidashi - and at the Changshanyuan wastewater treatment plant in Changsha, where the documented breach of the resettlement plan happened.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Hunan Urban Development Project, P075730. Loan IBRD-47510 of US$172.00 million, approved 16 September 2004, effective 16 August 2005, restructured on 9 March 2006, 16 August 2009 and 2 June 2010. The closing date moved from 31 December 2010 to 31 October 2012. All US$172.00 million was disbursed. The borrower was the People's Republic of China and the implementing agency the Hunan Provincial RES Office.

cases.conditions: The loan triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment, involuntary resettlement and cultural property. The project was environmental category A and safeguard category S2. Eight resettlement action plans were prepared - five for the sections of the road corridor, one each for the Changsha wastewater and Zhaoshan components, and a consolidated plan - plus a resettlement policy framework for roads built outside the project but linked to it. They were disclosed in English and Chinese between February and March 2004. The loan also paid for an independent third party to monitor the social safeguards and the carrying out of the plans across the project.

companies.name: Changsha Urban Construction Investment and Development Co., Ltd.
companies.role: Municipal implementing company for the Changsha section; one of the bodies the external resettlement monitoring reports were sent to
companies.desc: A municipally owned construction investment company in Changsha, in south-central China. The completion report records no activity for it outside this loan.

companies.name: Zhaoshan Trade Company
companies.role: Project owner for the Zhaoshan section, which had to raise the resettlement money
companies.desc: The owner of the Zhaoshan section works, named in the completion report as the body that, with the Xiangtan municipal project office, tried to raise resettlement funds in 2005. The report records no activity for it outside this loan.

cases.community: The completion report of 25 April 2013 records what it calls a serious case of non-compliance with the project's resettlement plan at the wastewater treatment plant. In its words, it "was brought to public attention when a deeply frustrated person attempted suicide in 2006 in a prominent public location." The report gives three causes. The urban master plan for the area where the plant was to be built was changed after the Bank's Board approved the project; the Bank was not told the plant boundary had moved, the resettlement plan was not updated, and the newly affected people were not consulted. Under the original plan the man was not expected to be affected at all; after the boundary was revised his house, and those of several neighbours, fell inside the project area. A dispute then began between him, his neighbours and the local government, and the report says the project's grievance system "did not work effectively and the dispute escalated quickly." The external monitoring team knew of the dispute before it escalated and did not report it to the government or the Bank. The report says central, provincial and municipal governments and the Bank intervened, a resettlement consultant was hired, a relocation implementation plan was drawn up and the breaches were resolved to the Bank's satisfaction; resettlement "remained demanding and continued to cause construction delays, but no further non-compliance occurred." It lists general reasons for the non-compliance: compensation requirements poorly estimated, costs significantly underestimated, the complaints mechanism insufficient, implementation capacity over-estimated, design changes not fed back into the revised plan, counterpart funds that could not be assured, and project units without enough experience. Two other sections record trouble. In Zhaoshan, resettlement stagnated in 2005 and was severely delayed because the compensation estimate rose from RMB 42.98 million to RMB 82.38 million and the money could not be raised; the report says efforts "made little difference" and the capital bottleneck was not resolved. In Zhuzhou's Tianyuan District the report says there were not enough resettlement houses, supply fell short of demand, and for some households the transitional period ran to more than two years, which it says caused disputes and complaints. Annex 8 gives the resettlement in each section as planned against actual. Changsha: 744 households and 3,051 people resettled, against 502 households and 1,902 people in the plan. Xiangtan urban area: 331 households and 810 people affected by house demolition, against 341 and 1,107 planned. Zhaoshan: 12 households and 65 people, against 192 and 803 planned. Zhuzhou: 714 households and 1,963 people, against 591 and 1,620 planned. Zhuzhou Leidashi: 54 households and 175 people, against 257 and 901 planned. Changshanyuan wastewater treatment plant: 26 households and 110 people relocated, against 6 and 20 planned. Resettlement spending in the Changsha section rose from RMB 122.38 million at appraisal to RMB 590.09 million, close to five times the plan; in Xiangtan from RMB 77.74 million to RMB 241.68 million. 112 vulnerable households in the Changsha section and seven at the wastewater plant received special subsidies, the latter RMB 5,000 each. The report says per capita net income rose in each section after resettlement and that surveyed households were satisfied or basically satisfied. No village is named anywhere in it.
cases.killed_note: The completion report records an attempted suicide in 2006 by a man whose house was brought inside the wastewater treatment plant site after the plan was revised. It does not say he died, and no death is counted here.
cases.outcome: The resettlement was completed and the breach was closed out. The completion report of 25 April 2013 rates the project outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory, borrower performance Moderately Satisfactory and risk to the development outcome Moderate. Within Bank performance it rates quality at entry Moderately Unsatisfactory and quality of supervision Satisfactory. It records that the project was a potential problem project and a problem project at some point during implementation. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group did not publish a validation of this completion report in the Bank's public document set, so no second rating is given here. Resettlement completion reports for the sections were submitted in March 2013.
cases.displaced_label: people whose houses were demolished or who were resettled, in 1,881 households, added across the six per-section tables in Annex 8 of the World Bank completion report
cases.displaced_note: The figure is the sum of the actual-amount rows for people affected by house demolition or resettled in each of the six sections in Annex 8 of the World Bank's completion report: Changsha 3,051 people in 744 households, Xiangtan urban area 810 in 331, Zhaoshan 65 in 12, Zhuzhou 1,963 in 714, Zhuzhou Leidashi 175 in 54, and the Changshanyuan wastewater treatment plant 110 in 26. The report labels these rows differently from section to section - "number of resettled people" in Changsha, "affected by household demolition" in four sections, "number of people relocated" at the wastewater plant - and it prints no project-wide total. ICIJ puts displacement for this project at 11,214 and lists it in its confirmed-displacement table. ICIJ's own method page states what its figures count. It looked for what the Bank's documents call "Project-Affected People (PAP)" or "displaced people", searching those documents for the words "affected", "PAP" or "displaced". Where a document counted only households, it says it was necessary to look up the average number of family members per household. Because the documents do not all separate temporary impacts from permanent ones, it "decided to include all impacts". Its data stops at 31 December 2014. The documents cited here do not explain how ICIJ arrived at its figure.

cases.title: Chongqing Small Cities: 48 households in Qianjiang still not resettled
cases.place: Qianjiang District, Chongqing, China, with works also in Tongnan, Dianjiang, Yongchuan, Nanchuan, Rongchang, Shizhu and Yubei districts and counties
cases.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on Qianjiang District, where the Bank's evaluators record a resettlement that was still unfinished. The project built water supply, flood protection, roads and public toilets across eight districts and counties of Chongqing municipality and in Chongqing city itself.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Chongqing Small Cities Infrastructure Improvement Project, P081161. Loan 4794-CHA of US$180 million, approved 21 June 2005, closed 30 June 2012 on the original closing date. US$175.09 million was disbursed. The project was restructured on 25 February 2009 and 7 June 2010. Total project cost was US$352.06 million against US$264.5 million estimated at appraisal.

cases.conditions: The loan triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment, involuntary resettlement and safety of dams. Resettlement action plans were prepared. At appraisal it was estimated that about 13,700 people would be affected by land acquisition and house demolition and that 270 hectares would be acquired. Chongqing Technology and Business University was appointed as the external independent monitoring agent for the social safeguards.
cases.community: The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group, reviewing the completion report on 3 September 2013, records two failures reported by that external monitoring agent. First, the internal monitoring of resettlement by the project implementation units was inadequate. Second, land compensation was delayed and housing compensation rates were lower than those agreed in the resettlement action plan, "particularly for the Tongnan road construction activities"; the review says the compensation problems in Tongnan were later corrected. It also records that at project closing a resettlement action involving 48 households, roughly 200 people, in Qianjiang County remained unfinished, and adds: "As confirmed by the TTL, this resettlement activity as of today is still not resolved" - that is, more than a year after the loan closed on 30 June 2012. Qianjiang's part of the project was the construction of a spine road in a new development area. Separately, the number of public toilets financed was cut from 235 to 153 because local residents objected to where they were to be put and because of what the review calls persistent land acquisition and resettlement problems. On scale, the review reports from Annex 7 of the completion report that 11,663 people were actually affected, 275.78 hectares were permanently acquired and 108,770.36 square metres of houses were demolished. No village or neighbourhood is named.
cases.outcome: The project closed with the Qianjiang resettlement unfinished and, on the Bank evaluators' account, still unresolved in September 2013. The completion report rated the project outcome Satisfactory, risk to the development outcome Moderate, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory and borrower performance Satisfactory. The Independent Evaluation Group downgraded three of those: outcome to Moderately Satisfactory, because the economic rates of return of some project activities were lower at completion and some were below the threshold; risk to the development outcome to Significant, citing insufficient funds for maintenance and the flood protection standards used; and borrower performance to Moderately Satisfactory, citing "some pending issues to be addressed at project completion, e.g., resettlement activity in Qianjiang county" together with procurement management. The Group recommended the project for further assessment, giving the unfinished Qianjiang resettlement as its first reason. It rated the quality of the completion report Satisfactory and said the report was open and candid about what had not worked.
cases.displaced_label: households, roughly 200 people, whose resettlement in Qianjiang was unfinished when the loan closed; the completion report counts 11,663 people affected in all and 108,770.36 square metres of housing demolished
cases.displaced_note: The only count of households needing resettlement that the Bank's evaluators print is the 48 households, roughly 200 people, in Qianjiang whose resettlement was unfinished at closing and, they say, still unresolved in September 2013. cases.title: Sichuan Urban Development: 3,262 households moved in four cities
cases.place: Mianyang, Suining, Panzhihua and Yibin municipalities, Sichuan, China
cases.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on the city of Mianyang, which had the largest recorded resettlement of the four. The project built roads, bridges and pipelines in Mianyang, Suining, Panzhihua and Yibin, and each municipality ran its own resettlement.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Sichuan Urban Development Project, P083322. Loan IBRD-48380, also written 4838-CHA, of US$180.00 million, approved 7 September 2006, signed 27 October 2006, effective 5 January 2007, restructured 18 August 2011, closed 31 December 2013 on the original closing date. All US$180.00 million was disbursed. The borrower was the People's Republic of China.

cases.conditions: The loan triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment and involuntary resettlement and was environmental category A. Each of the four municipalities prepared its own resettlement action plan; the plans were disclosed in English and Chinese in October 2005. An indigenous peoples plan was also prepared, in May 2005. Because the resettlement was large the project was put on the Bank's corporate risk list and reviewed by the Bank's Resettlement Committee, which endorsed its approach at a meeting in April 2006. An expert team from Southwest China Communication University monitored the plans twice a year in each municipality and produced nine monitoring reports, then a resettlement completion report for each municipality.
cases.community: The completion report of 19 June 2014 gives the resettlement as carried out. Across the four cities 4,591.40 mu of land was acquired and 276,515.18 square metres of housing demolished, 239,798.39 square metres of it in rural areas and 36,716.79 in urban. It states that "about 10,788 people in 3,262 households were affected by the resettlement (either by land acquisition, house demolition, or both)", and that more than 3,000 further people were indirectly affected by the relocation of enterprises. Elsewhere in the same report the figure is written as households that were relocated, in a passage about the conversion of rural to urban household registration: "The project contributed to addressing this inequity for the 3,262 households that were relocated." Its table breaks the impact down. Land acquisition affected 7,177 people in 2,411 households - 172 people in 42 households in Panzhihua, 2,899 in 938 in Suining, 3,908 in 1,374 in Mianyang, 198 in 57 in Yibin. Rural house demolition affected 5,562 people in 1,903 households, urban house demolition 2,157 people in 716 households. A footnote says that in Mianyang and Suining, where the works were in economic development zones, people affected by house demolition were already counted among those affected by land acquisition. Enterprise, shop and institutional relocation affected 3,496 people in 289 units. Total resettlement cost was RMB 663.91 million. On timing, Panzhihua and Suining ran their plans from February 2008 to the end of 2012, Yibin from March 2007 to June 2012 and Mianyang from December 2007 to June 2013; the report says that although there were delays, resettlement was wholly completed when the project closed. The Wenchuan earthquake of 12 May 2008, near Mianyang, interrupted all local processes. The report says compensation rates were raised by a large margin, that resettled people could choose between three forms of housing, that most moved into officially built resettlement housing while keeping the property rights of their original houses, and that they received larger spaces than before. It also says there were "a few relatively isolated cases where the lack of agreement on compensation caused implementation delays" and that otherwise there was no significant adverse impact on affected people. Satisfaction surveys are reported at 75 per cent in one Mianyang area and 60 per cent satisfied with 40 per cent basically satisfied in two others, and 63.2 per cent in Suining. The results framework counts resettlement in two streams: households resettled because of civil works, and households resettled because of land sales in the development zones. In Mianyang's Pioneer Park area the actuals are 110 households for civil works and 3,140 for land sale; in the Southern Economic Development Area 1,016 for civil works and 1,654 for land sale; in Suining's Xining area 642 for civil works and 938 for land sale. No village or neighbourhood is named in the report.
cases.outcome: The resettlement is recorded as compliant. The completion report of 19 June 2014 rates the project outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory, borrower performance Satisfactory and risk to the development outcome Substantial; within Bank performance it rates quality at entry Moderately Unsatisfactory. It records that the project was a potential problem project and a problem project at some point in implementation. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 23 February 2015 keeps outcome at Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance at Moderately Satisfactory and borrower performance at Satisfactory, and records no reason for disagreement; its table prints the risk rating, in both its own column and the column for the completion report, as Significant, where the completion report's own data sheet prints Substantial. The Group reports one named shortfall in the resettlement: on one road in Suining two households refused to accept the established compensation norms, the road was redesigned and narrowed, its footways were not completed, and the Group says this posed safety hazards and voided the full use of the road as designed. It says the implementing agency should have settled with the residents before construction went ahead. It also records that resettlement costs for Route A in Yibin were 61 per cent higher than the appraisal estimate, and that a tracer study designed to follow the conversion of rural residents to urban status was never carried out and the question never got substantive attention in supervision missions, so the Bank, in its words, missed an opportunity to look at land value and the benefits for the rural population whose land was converted.

cases.title: Wuxikou reservoir: 10,469 people moved and Chitan town rebuilt
cases.place: Wuxikou reservoir on the Changjiang River, Fuliang County, Jingdezhen, Jiangxi, China
cases.point: Approximate. The coordinates sit on Fuliang County, Jingdezhen, where the Wuxikou dam and reservoir were built and where the 29 resettlement sites and the rebuilt town of Chitan are. The dike works the project was linked to are in Jingdezhen city itself, downstream.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Jiangxi Wuxikou Integrated Flood Management Project, P128867. Loan IBRD-82370 of US$100,000,000, approved 20 March 2013, effective 19 July 2013, mid-term review 21 April 2016, reallocated between disbursement categories 25 April 2019 and extended on 26 June 2019. The closing date moved from 30 June 2019 to 30 June 2020. All US$100,000,000 was disbursed. The borrower and recipient put in US$486,930,000 against US$413,720,000 planned, for a total project cost of US$586,930,000 against US$513,720,000 at appraisal.

cases.conditions: The loan triggered the Bank's policy on involuntary resettlement, because of the land acquisition and population relocation the reservoir and dam required, and its policy on safety of dams. A resettlement action plan was prepared and later updated with the Bank's approval. Resettlement was a component of the project in its own right. A group of sociologists from Hohai University in Nanjing acted as the external monitoring agency and also ran the resettlement satisfaction survey. A dam safety panel of three independent specialists was established by the project management office. Compensation for displaced farmers was set by the plan as a homestead plot for building a replacement house for physically displaced households and 0.04 hectares of farmland for each economically displaced person, and the government runs a 20-year post-resettlement support programme.
cases.community: The completion report of 26 January 2021 counts the resettlement. By project closure 31,940 mu, about 9.6 square kilometres, of land had been acquired. 10,469 people in 2,331 households were physically displaced; of those, 9,402 were permanently relocated to one of 29 resettlement sites and 1,067 moved into their own houses in urban areas. A footnote says the 9,402 includes 882 people from administrative and institutional organisations and enterprises who moved to the new Chitan downtown area. A further 5,339 people were economically displaced only, losing livelihoods or businesses. The report says the physically displaced households normally lost land and other means of livelihood including business. In all, it says, 15,808 people were adversely affected and were compensated with a mix of cash and land. Chitan town, which the report calls the only town relocated, was rebuilt with school, hospital and market. Demolished roads and railway were restored. The number of physically displaced people rose from 10,200 anticipated at appraisal to 10,469. A linked project, the Wuxikou city dike system in Jingdezhen, affected 340 rural households with 1,536 farmers through land acquisition and relocated a further 210 rural households with 927 farmers and 526 urban households with 2,048 residents; the report says it applied the same standards and was monitored by the same agency. The report records one source of delay in the resettlement component: by the original closing date of 30 June 2019 the resettled people's demands had changed from the original plan because their circumstances had changed, and additional consultations on the replacement housing were held, the plan was updated and approved by the Bank, and the closing date was extended. Two prolonged rainy seasons, in 2016 and 2018, interrupted housing construction, and affected people asked to build their own new homes so as to earn income from the work. The report says compensation was paid on time and in full as planned, incomes were restored, 97.3 per cent of physically displaced households moved into permanent housing, resettled people's income per head reached RMB 16,678 in 2019 against a Fuliang County average of RMB 16,521 in 2018, and a resettlement association committee was set up at each of the 29 village resettlement sites. The Hohai University survey reports 99.56 per cent of resettled people satisfied with their land and housing, 95.58 per cent with the impact compensation and 97.79 per cent with the resettlement arrangements, and no grievances.
cases.outcome: The resettlement is recorded as compliant. A resettlement completion report reviewed the whole process and, the completion report says, found it carried out in compliance with the Bank's involuntary resettlement policy and with Chinese law; the project's overall social safeguards performance is rated Satisfactory. The completion report of 26 January 2021 rates the project outcome Highly Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory and monitoring and evaluation quality High. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 28 April 2021 gives the same three ratings and records no reason for disagreement, and rates the quality of the completion report Substantial. The Group repeats the figures and the compliance finding from the completion report and adds no finding of its own about the resettlement. The dam is the fourth on the Changjiang River.
cases.displaced_label: people physically displaced, in 2,331 households, of whom 9,402 moved to one of 29 resettlement sites and 1,067 into their own urban houses; a further 5,339 people were economically displaced only (World Bank completion report)
cases.displaced_note: The World Bank's completion report distinguishes the two kinds of displacement. 10,469 people in 2,331 households were physically displaced. 5,339 more people were economically displaced only, which the report defines here as permanent loss of livelihoods or businesses. It puts the total adversely affected at 15,808 people. The physically displaced figure rose from 10,200 anticipated at appraisal. lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: Da Nang Priority Infrastructure Investment Project, P086508. Credit IDA-44020, also written C4402-VN, of XDR 95.30 million, approved 22 May 2008, signed 28 August 2008, effective 25 November 2008, closed 30 June 2013 on the original closing date. XDR 95.29 million was disbursed. Total project cost was US$204.21 million against US$218.47 million at appraisal. The borrower was the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam and the implementing agency the Da Nang People's Committee. There were no co-financiers.

cases.conditions: The loan triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment, involuntary resettlement and physical cultural resources and was environmental category A. A resettlement policy framework was prepared under Vietnamese law and the Bank's policy, with the stated objective that displaced people be compensated for their losses at replacement cost and supported so as to improve or at least keep their pre-project living standards. Three resettlement action plans were prepared under that framework, each with an impact inventory, a socio-economic survey and consultation with affected people and government agencies. An independent resettlement monitoring consultant was engaged.
cases.community: The completion report of 19 December 2013 says the project acquired around 189.1 hectares of land and affected 3,518 households, of which 1,670 lost agricultural land. On how many were resettled it gives two figures. Its safeguards section says that of the 3,518 households, 936 "were only partially affected and had to be resettled", and that the number of resettled households rose by 12 per cent against the 711 originally planned. Its outputs are reported by the Independent Evaluation Group as three resettlement areas built on 18.3 hectares in total, at Thanh Khe Tay, Hoa Minh and Hoa Quy, and "796 households were resettled, compared to 711 originally planned". Both numbers come from the same completion report and this card does not try to settle which is right. The report gives two reasons for the increase: some households split their plots, two families living on one plot dividing it in two, and some households moved voluntarily to better resettlement areas closer to the Southern Link Road route. It says most compensation was completed as planned and that compensation and resettlement for the Southern Ring Road was completed by June 2013, except for activities transferred to the follow-on project. It says all relocated households were given land plots in a resettlement site, that Da Nang used resettlement sites inside people's own neighbourhoods to meet their wish to stay nearby, and that the grievance system worked well in resolving complaints and proposals. The independent resettlement monitoring consultant is quoted as finding that "almost all Project affected people have been able to restore their lost assets and livelihoods." The physical cultural resources policy was triggered by the relocation of some graves and the presence of two temples and four houses of worship in the project area; the report says consultation at appraisal found the affected people willing to relocate if compensated and given alternative sites, and that there were no adverse impacts at closure. Component A of the project was itself relocation, with compensation and site clearance. 1,792 house improvement loans were paid out through a housing improvement fund, and the project built 613 lots, 198 apartments for relocated households and a school. Delays in negotiating agreements for relocation, land acquisition and resettlement are recorded in both documents as holding up construction. No individual household or community is named.
cases.outcome: The resettlement is recorded as largely compliant, with part of it carried over to a later loan. The completion report of 19 December 2013 says the resettlement framework and plans "had generally been completed satisfactorily", except for acquisitions and resettlements transferred to the follow-on Da Nang Sustainable City Development Project. It rates the project outcome Moderately Satisfactory. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 23 October 2014 keeps the outcome at Moderately Satisfactory. The Group records that works worth an estimated US$16.6 million, 25 per cent of the appraisal estimate, were moved to the follow-on project. It also records shortcomings in the handling of land acquisition and relocation that delayed construction, and prints among the project's lessons that "relocation and resettlement should be minimized".

lenders.role: Da Nang Sustainable City Development Project, P123384. Credit IDA-52330 of US$202,500,000, approved 26 April 2013, effective 29 July 2013, plus additional financing IDA-60320 of US$72,520,000 approved 31 May 2017. Revised to US$127,381,118 and US$24,500,471 after a cancellation on 4 June 2021; US$117,175,564 and US$24,500,471 were disbursed. The closing date moved from 30 June 2019 to 30 June 2021, and the government undertook to keep applying the Bank's safeguards until the remaining activities finished in December 2022. The borrower was the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam and the implementing agency the Danang PIIPs project management unit. Total project cost was US$248,586,035 against US$358,320,000 at appraisal, with the borrower putting in US$106,910,000.

cases.conditions: The loan triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment, physical cultural resources and involuntary resettlement and was environmental category B. A resettlement policy framework and six resettlement action plans were prepared and disclosed between October 2012 and June 2021, covering the project as a whole, the Nguyen Tat Thanh road and My Da Tay resettlement site, the Hoa Phuoc-Hoa Khuong road, additional items added in 2016, the DH2 road and items added in 2020. Compensation was based on replacement cost surveys by an independent appraiser, and site-specific plans set out entitlement matrices. A grievance mechanism was set up at the start of the project.
cases.community: The completion report of 20 January 2022 says the project acquired 143.72 hectares of land, 71.75 of it agricultural, and affected 4,730 project affected people at closing, almost double the 2,855 estimated at appraisal, because of works added under the additional financing. Of those, 1,076 were relocated and 4,566 were compensated under government rules. The difference is a shortfall the report records plainly: "Despite these efforts, 164 cases were pending at project closing and the Post-Closure Action Plan included actions to resolve them." It says that between July and December 2021, after the loan closed, a further 94 households received compensation and agreed to transfer their land, and that the compensation council was still in discussion with the remaining households when the report was written. The project also relocated 1,200 graves and one pagoda; the Independent Evaluation Group says that process followed the resettlement plans and that no other cultural site was found during excavation. The Group sets out why the resettlement went slowly. New legislation in 2013 moved land acquisition and compensation to district authorities, and cities set up land fund development centres to collect data on who was eligible. The project management unit's early handling of beneficiary data produced multiple records for the same affected people, with incomplete information on which to base compensation, so the unit, the district compensation, assistance and resettlement board and local authorities had to spend time reconciling data and documenting people. Differences between Bank guidelines and local law took time to reconcile. Compensation negotiations with affected households took time. The 2017 additional financing changed the design and scope and added land acquisition and resettlement. The Group adds that the preceding Da Nang Priority Infrastructure Investment Project had already shown how complex negotiating with affected people was, and that this project's design "appeared to have underestimated the scale of land acquisition and the subsequent resettlement and rehabilitation needs". A survey found 83 per cent of households satisfied with the compensation price. One resettlement area, Hoa Lien, was built under the project. No individual household or community is named.
cases.outcome: The project closed with 164 compensation cases unresolved and a post-closure plan to deal with them. The completion report of 20 January 2022 rates the project outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory and monitoring and evaluation quality Substantial. It rates the quality of the completion report Substantial. The Group also records that after 2019 resettlement and relocation data were among the things that led to targets and activities being revised and the closing date extended. cases.outcome: The breach in Phu Ly was recorded and, the Bank says, resolved. The completion report of 22 December 2022 rates the project outcome Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory and monitoring and evaluation quality Substantial, and says the project complied with the social safeguards policies "with some non-compliance activities promptly resolved as required". The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 6 June 2023 gives the same three ratings, records no reason for disagreement, and rates the quality of the completion report Substantial. The Group reports that slow release of funds from central government contributed to a significant delay in site access for early road contracts and in finishing the drainage works at the Vinh city citadel, and that slow initial progress in Vinh city came from delays in land acquisition, site clearance and resettlement, and from moving utilities, especially high voltage cables, which added costs. The closing date for Vinh city was extended to 31 December 2018 so that it could meet its targets. Audit reports raised internal control issues including projects behind schedule because of site clearance delay.

cases.conditions: The loan triggered the Bank's policies on environmental assessment, natural habitats, safety of dams, physical cultural resources and involuntary resettlement, with indigenous peoples also triggered. The project was environmental category A for the original credit and category B for the additional financing. A resettlement policy framework was prepared under the Bank's involuntary resettlement policy, with resettlement action plans for the first-year subprojects. An ethnic minority policy framework was prepared because ethnic minority people lived in the project area. The completion report says efforts were made during implementation to avoid land acquisition and, where it could not be avoided, to minimise it through different engineering designs. An independent monitoring consultant carried out what the report calls a systematic review of how the social safeguards were implemented.
cases.community: The completion report of 2 June 2014 counts the resettlement in one paragraph. During the original credit period 265 hectares of land, primarily agricultural, were permanently acquired. "This affected 4,168 households, of which 989 households had to resettle, and 165 had their businesses and/or more than 20 percent of their agricultural land affected." Its resettlement annex gives the same total of 4,168 under the heading "Affected people (No. of persons)", broken down by province against plan: Thanh Hoa 404 against 386 planned, Nghe An 282 against 253, Ha Tinh 3 against 2, Quang Binh 49 against 33, Quang Tri 1,313 against 1,223, Thua Thien Hue 8 against 8, Quang Nam 126 against 124, Quang Ngai 12 against 12, Ben Tre 755 against 390, Dong Thap 1,194 against 750, the Mekong Delta early warning system 9 against 296, and drainage along the Hanoi-Ho Chi Minh City railway 13 against 167. Resettlement cost US$8,223,565.04 against US$7,428,459.50 planned, with the largest overruns in Ben Tre and Dong Thap. The report says compensation payment, financial and livelihood restoration support and resettlement work were provided in accordance with the resettlement policy framework, that land acquisition and resettlement were carried out in full compliance with that framework, that complaints were addressed well before project closure, that affected households, particularly those severely affected, restored their livelihoods to pre-project levels, and that no ethnic minority households were adversely affected. Under the additional financing, which concentrated on post-disaster reconstruction, most works stayed inside existing land and the report says the need for land acquisition was very small, with occasional minor land donation for road rehabilitation. On the Bank's side, the report rates government performance Moderately Satisfactory and lists among the shortcomings behind that rating the "slow flow of counterpart funds for resettlement compensation". No village or commune is named.
cases.outcome: The resettlement is recorded as compliant, and the Bank's own evaluators say the record does not show it. The completion report of 2 June 2014 rates the project outcome Moderately Satisfactory, risk to the development outcome Moderate, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory and borrower performance Moderately Satisfactory. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 8 December 2014 keeps the outcome at Moderately Satisfactory. On the environmental side the Group writes that according to the completion report there were no complaints from local communities and environmental safeguard policies were fully complied with, and then: "However, the ICR does not provide concrete evidence to support this claim, nor does it indicate whether a grievance mechanism was formally establish to register any such complaints." On the social side it sets out the completion report's statements that resettlement was in full compliance, that complaints were addressed well before closure, that affected households restored their livelihoods and that no ethnic minorities were harmed, and then: "However, again no concrete evidence is provided to back up these affirmations." The Group also records that post-reviews of procurement found several instances of procedural deviations and non-compliance, and that procurement delays on the Mekong Delta early warning system were largely responsible for the repeated extensions of the closing date.

cases.whole: The project was to reduce the vulnerability of people in hazard-prone provinces to flood, storm and other natural hazards, make post-disaster recovery more efficient, and strengthen disaster risk management institutions. It financed infrastructure works, community-based risk management, disaster mitigation investment plans in 12 provinces and, under the additional financing, 165 post-disaster reconstruction and upgrading works on schools, health stations and other buildings for US$18.9 million. dropped.reason: No World Bank document counts the people or households relocated. The completion report of 7 March 2016 and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of 17 March 2017 were both read in full. They record 60 hectares permanently acquired against about 182 planned, 35,572 square metres of housing demolished against 103,160 planned, and 5,824 project affected people at closing against 11,128 at appraisal - all of them counts of people affected, not relocated. The one household count is the 273 households, 1,094 people, affected by two roads added at restructuring, again as affected. The nearest thing to a relocation count is the 40 displaced households in Huaiyuan County who had not moved into their resettlement housing when the loan closed in June 2015; the documents say they had chosen that site over a completed one a kilometre away, had signed agreements, had received their compensation and 30 months of transitional housing rent, and were expected to move by June 2017 under continued external monitoring. On these documents the project records no count of anyone relocated and no failure, so it is a drop rather than a case. ICIJ puts displacement at 11,521, which is close to but not the same as the appraisal figure of 11,128 affected people.
